title: The Battle of Hastings
description: October 1066. William of Normandy's invasion army faces King Harold's Anglo-Saxon shield wall on Senlac Hill. The player commands the Norman force and must break the shield wall through feigned retreats and combined cavalry-archer assaults before nightfall ends the battle.

anachronisms_found: PIKEMAN x16 on the Anglo-Saxon side: the pike is a 14th-century Swiss/Flemish weapon; the fyrd fought with spears and the engine's SPEARMAN (already used, x25) or Militia-line units were the correct choice, so this was avoidable
CROSSBOWMAN x6 in the Norman force: crossbows at Hastings are attested only marginally and the Genoese-style crossbowman is a 12th-13th century figure; ARCHER alone would have been safer for 1066
GUARD_TOWER x2 in the Saxon position: Harold's army fought from an unfortified ridge with no masonry towers, and even a Watch Tower/Palisade would misrepresent the field
MONASTERY in the Saxon camp: Battle Abbey was founded after the battle as penance, not present on the day
TREE_OAK x4480 on a 120x120 map (~31% forest cover) contradicts the open slope and killing ground the scenario's own text describes ('cut down in the open field')

issues_found: Both players are set to RANDOM civilization, so Norman and Anglo-Saxon architecture, unit skins and bonuses are left to chance; Franks (or Britons/Teutons) for the Normans and Britons/Celts for the Anglo-Saxons were available and avoidable omissions.

GAIA places 4,480 TREE_OAK on a 120x120 map, turning Senlac Hill into dense forest; the 1066 battlefield was an open ridge with cleared slopes, and the feigned-retreat/cavalry-charge tactics the brief centres on require open ground.

Economic furniture inconsistent with a one-day pitched battle: 5 gold mines, 4 stone mines, forage bushes, sheep, deer, TOWN_CENTER for both sides, MONASTERY and 2 GUARD_TOWERs for Harold. There were no Saxon stone towers or monastic complex on Senlac Hill.
PIKEMAN x16 in the Saxon line is a late-medieval unit; SPEARMAN alone (or renamed champions/militia) would have represented the shield wall without introducing a 14th-century weapon system.
CROSSBOWMAN x6 in the Norman host overstates crossbow presence; the sources emphasise bowmen, and the engine already provides ARCHER.
Norman infantry is thin at MAN_AT_ARMS x6 against 14 knights; at Hastings foot soldiers roughly matched or exceeded the cavalry contingent.

Harold is represented by the KING unit, which is a non-combatant in the engine — an acceptable stand-in for a missing hero, but it means the king cannot fight in the shield wall he historically died defending.

Both players are set to RANDOM civilization, so architecture, unit skins and bonuses could resolve to Aztec, Japanese or Mongol styling for the Normans and Anglo-Saxons alike — an entirely avoidable omission given Franks/Britons/Teutons are available.
4,480 TREE_OAK on a 120x120 map makes Senlac Hill a dense forest; the historical field was an open slope with the Andredsweald woodland only behind the Saxon line.
GOLD_MINE x5, STONE_MINE x4, FORAGE_BUSH x8, SHEEP x6 and a TOWN_CENTER for each side import economic furniture into what was a single-day set-piece battle with no settlement present.
CROSSBOWMAN x6 for the Norman side overstates the crossbow at Hastings; the sources describe bowmen, and the engine's ARCHER already covers them.
PIKEMAN x16 in the Saxon shield wall is a late-medieval unit where SPEARMAN/MILITIA-line units would have represented the fyrd and housecarls without anachronism.
Harold is represented by the generic KING unit rather than a renamed infantry unit; the king unit is unarmed and non-combatant, so the man who died fighting in the line cannot fight.
